questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Fear of closed spaces
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Claustrophobia"** means an extreme or irrational fear of confined places. (संकीर्ण स्थानों का भय)

 
 
• **Example: **She refused to get into the elevator due to her** claustrophobia.**
 
 
 
• **"Claustrophobia"** refers to the fear of closed or confined spaces. (संकीर्ण स्थानों का भय)
 
 
• **Example: **His **claustrophobia **made it difficult for him to travel in the crowded subway.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct one-word substitute for **"Fear of closed spaces"** is **'Claustrophobia'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Photophobia **(प्रकाश का भय): An abnormal fear or intolerance of light.

 
 
• **Example:** His migraine was accompanied by photophobia, making it difficult for him to be in bright environments.
 
 
 
• **Optophobia **(आंखें खोलने का भय): Fear of opening one's eyes.
 
 
• **Example: **After the traumatic event, he developed optophobia and often kept his eyes closed.
 
 
 
• **Agoraphobia **(खुले स्थान का भय): Fear of open or crowded spaces.
 
 
• **Example:** She rarely left her house due to her agoraphobia.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Historians tell us how this country was divided into three.

options.text: We are told by historians how this country has been divided into three.
We are told by historians how this country divided into three.
We are told by historians how this country was divided into three.
We have been told by historians how this country was divided into three.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary task is to convert the given sentence into **passive voice **while retaining its original meaning.
 
• The given sentence is: "**Historians tell us how this country was divided into three.**"
 
• In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The correct passive sentence is: "**We are told by historians how this country was divided into three.**"

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"We are told by historians how this country was divided into three."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "We are told by historians how this country has been divided into three." - This changes the tense of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 2:** "We are told by historians how this country divided into three." - This is grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 4:** "We have been told by historians how this country was divided into three." - This changes the tense of the original sentence.

questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to

form a meaningful sentence.

(P) technology has revolutionised

(Q) and it has transformed the way

(O) every aspect of our lives

(R) we communicate and connect
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To form a meaningful sentence, it is essential to begin with the subject and then logically follow with the statement that provides **a coherent idea**.
 
• **Part (P)** "technology has revolutionised" serves as the beginning of the sentence, introducing the subject 'technology' and stating its impact.
 
• **Part (O)** "every aspect of our lives" follows next, describing what has been revolutionised by technology.
 
• **Part (Q)** "and it has transformed the way" continues by explaining the specific transformation caused by technology.
 
• **Part (R)** "we communicate and connect" completes the sentence by specifying the areas that have been transformed by technology.
 
• Therefore, the correct sequence is **POQR**, forming the sentence: "Technology has revolutionised every aspect of our lives and it has transformed the way we communicate and connect."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (RPQO):** This option starts with a phrase that does not introduce the subject correctly and leads to a sentence that lacks coherence.
 
• **Option 2 (RPOQ):** This option misplaces parts of the sentence, creating a grammatically incorrect and unclear structure.
 
• **Option 4 (ORQP):** Starting with "every aspect of our lives" disrupts the logical flow of the sentence, making it awkward and unclear.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The company will launch the new product next month, and they are already promoting it through various marketing channels.

options.text: The new product will be launched by the company next month, and it is already being promoted through various marketing channels.
The new product were been launched by the company next month, and it already was promoting through various marketing channels.
The new product was launched by the company next month, and it is already promoted through various marketing channels.
The new product will have been launched by the company next month, and it was already being promoted through various marketing channels.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct **passive voice** construction involves changing the object of the** active sentence** into the subject of the **passive sentence.**
 
• The new subjec**t (the new product)** is followed by the appropriate form of the verb** "to be" (will be)** and the **past participle of the main verb (launched).**
 
• The second part of the sentence also needs to be in passive voice:** "it is already being promoted."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The new product will be launched by the company next month, and it is already being promoted through various marketing channels."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** Contains incorrect verb forms "were been" and "was promoting," making it grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 3:** Uses incorrect future tense "was launched" and does not use passive voice correctly in the second part.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect future perfect tense "will have been launched" and incorrect past continuous "was already being promoted."

The media, these days, constructs _______ (misleading) narratives on politics and celebrities to increase the viewership.
questions.solution:

• **Example: **The statement he made was true and verifiable.

• **Example:** She gave a candid interview about her experiences.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The group of travellers were wonderstruck by the _________ of the coin.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is identifying the correct characteristic of the coin that would leave the travellers wonderstruck.
 
• Options such as "wait", "white", and "wide" do not fit logically in the context of being a characteristic of a coin.
 
• The term "weight" is the most appropriate option as it logically fits the context of a coin having a notable characteristic that could leave someone wonderstruck.
 
• Thus, the correct option to fill in the blank is **"weight".**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The group of travellers were wonderstruck by the **weight** __of the coin."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "wait" **– This option is not relevant in the context of describing a coin.
 
• **Option 2: "white" **– This option describes color, which is not as striking for a coin as weight might be.
 
• **Option 3: "wide" **– This option might describe the size but doesn't fit as well in the context as "weight".
 
• **Option 4: "weight" **– **This option is the most logical and appropriate choice for the given context.**

questions.question:
Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence.

They could (always) stay in, or go for a walk.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"always"** means at all times; on all occasions. (हमेशा)

 
 
• **Example: **She **always** arrives at work early.
 
 
 
• **"Either"** refers to one or the other of two things or people. (या तो)
 
 
• **Example: **You can **either** call me at home or at the office.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct replacement for **'always'** in this context is **'either'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Had better **(अच्छा होगा): Indicates advice or a suggestion about what someone should do.

 
 
• **Example:** You had better finish your homework before going out.
 
 
 
• **Not only **(न केवल): Used to indicate that something is true and that there is more to be said about it.
 
 
• **Example: **She is not only a great singer but also a talented dancer.
 
 
 
• **Neither** (न तो): Not the one nor the other of two people or things.
 
 
• **Example:** Neither of the two candidates was suitable for the job.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**whose**" is the correct option because it is a possessive pronoun used to indicate **that something belongs to or is associated with the person or people mentioned earlier, in this case, "children."**
 
• "**Which**" is a pronoun used for things, not people.
 
• "**Whom**" is an objective pronoun, used when referring to the object of a verb or preposition, which does not fit the possessive noun that is needed here.
 
• "**Who**" is a subjective pronoun used to refer to a person or people, but here we need the possessive form to indicate the weak learning of the children.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Children, whose__ basic, core learning (reading, math, languages, etc.) was weak to begin with, face a significant risk of regression.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Which (जो)**: used for things, not people.
 
• **Whom (जिसे/जिन्हें)**: objective pronoun used for a person, indicating them as the object of a verb or preposition.
 
• **Who (कौन/जिन्होंने)**: subjective pronoun used to refer to a person.
